## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical cache invalidation across two stores in a multi-tenant setting.

## Key Concepts
- Cache invalidation strategies (explicit vs TTL)
- Tenant-scoped keys and isolation
- Invalidation channels (pub/sub, Streams)
- Thundering herd avoidance (coalescing, locks)
- Version stamps and write-through options

// Publisher sketch
pub.publish('invalidate:tenant:' + tenantId, { key: 'tenant:' + tenantId + ':user:' + userId + ':profile' })

```javascript

  const key = 'tenant:' + tenantId + ':user:' + userId + ':profile'
  let val = await redis.get(key)
  if (val) return val
  // fetch from DB, then cache
}
```

- How would you test cross-store coherence and failure modes?

- TTL revocation checks

## Code Example
```javascript
// Token validation middleware (simplified)
function validateToken(req, res, next){
  const t = req.headers.authorization?.split(' ')[1]
  if(!t) return res.status(401).send({code:'unauthorized'})
  const payload = verifyJwt(t, { issuer:'https://idp/', audience:`tenant:${req.tenant}` })
  if(!payload || isRevoked(t)) return res.status(401).send({code:'unauthorized'})
  req.user = payload; next()
}
```
